Serial Tool Desktop User Guide

This guide describes the existing Windows-first Desktop controls for operators of COM or raw TCP devices.

Choose Your Interface

The Windows release includes two operator-facing executables. Choose the interface for your workflow.

Program Use
serial-tool.exe CLI commands, scripts, and automation.
Serial Tool.exe Desktop application for interactive COM/TCP communication.

This guide covers Desktop. For command-line instructions, open PowerShell in the release folder and run .\serial-tool.exe user-guide --lang en to open the bundled offline CLI guide.

Getting started

On Windows, install the system Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime. If it is missing, the application offers to open the official download page and exits without creating a Tauri window; it does not install WebView2. Start the built Serial Tool.exe or use npm run tauri -- dev from apps/desktop for development.

The main areas are Connection Setup, Terminal, and Sequence. Choose COM or TCP and Live or Simulation before connecting. Desktop Simulation uses only loopback-v1; periodic-rx-v1 is for Streaming Simulation Workers and is not a Desktop mode.

Language

The top-right Language control switches between English and Traditional Chinese without reloading. The displayed name is the current language. The selected language is remembered locally (serial-tool.locale); the first launch uses the WebView language preference, with English as fallback. Language and Appearance are independent. Appearance supports System, Light, and Dark modes. Switching language never changes device connectivity, terminal bytes, Sequence data, or exported file formats. Core/CLI/Worker diagnostics and machine-readable data are not translated.

Offline Help

Select Help at the top right to open the built-in offline guide in a separate window. It uses the current language (English or Traditional Chinese) and appearance (System, Light, or Dark). Help can switch language independently of the main window. Close and reopen Help to apply later changes to the main window's preferences. The guide works offline without requiring GitHub or other online resources.

Connection Setup: COM and TCP

In Connection Setup, choose COM Port or TCP/IP using the transport tabs. COM Port Live uses an explicit physical port; Refresh ports lists available ports and USB metadata without opening them. Set baud rate, data bits, parity, stop bits, flow control and timeout. In TCP/IP Live, enter a hostname, IPv4 or IPv6 address, device Port (1–65535), Connect Timeout (default 3000ms) and shared read/write I/O Timeout (default 1000ms). Host and Port are separate fields; do not enter an HTTP URL. TCP is a raw byte-stream client: it does not provide HTTP, frames, auto-reconnect, or a guarantee that DNS plus all address attempts complete within a single Connect Timeout.

The Connection options gear controls one shared Live/Simulation mode for both transports. Simulation uses deterministic loopback-v1, with no COM access, DNS lookup, or TCP socket; COM Port selection and TCP Host/Port are disabled but retain their values. TCP timeouts must remain valid in Simulation. The COM and TCP form values are separately retained when switching tabs, but neither is saved across app restarts. Numeric COM inputs retain native number semantics with hidden spin buttons; TCP Port/Timeout inputs preserve partial text while typing and validate on Connect.

Transport, connection settings and execution mode are locked while connecting, connected, running or disconnecting. The gear remains available to view the options; it closes on a second click, outside click or Escape (which restores focus). Hiding options does not reset the mode. The header shows COM Port or TCP/IP, mode, and the existing connection status. Incoming bytes are automatically received for either transport while connected.

Terminal transmission and Auto TX

Send Text transmits the exact UTF-8 bytes entered without adding CR or LF. Send Hex accepts ASCII whitespace and case-insensitive pairs of hex digits. Auto TX Source selects the Auto TX payload and defaults to Input. Input uses the Text/Hex payload; switching sources never clears the Send payload, because the same control also serves Manual Send. Start Auto TX sends the selected payload immediately, then repeats with the specified positive integer interval in milliseconds until Stop Auto TX or Disconnect. Each interval starts after the preceding send completes; delayed sends are not replayed in a burst. Continuous RX remains active. Payload source, payload, format, Auto TX file, and interval are locked while Auto TX runs. Manual Send, Send File, and Run Sequence are disabled until it stops; Disconnect, Display Mode, and Clear View remain available. A connection error stops Auto TX automatically. Start Auto TX requires a nonempty Text/Hex payload for Input or a selected file for File (Raw); the two sources are never combined and Core keeps other TX requests Busy while Auto TX runs.

Auto TX Source File (Raw) selects any file without restricting its extension and records only its path. Start Auto TX then reads the whole file once in the Rust backend and transmits that fixed byte snapshot, so the bytes are the same as Send File (Raw): no UTF-8 conversion, newline conversion, or hex-text parsing. Empty files, missing files, and unreadable files are rejected with an error and do not start Auto TX or reserve the connection. Editing the file while Auto TX runs has no effect; Stop and Start reads it again. Stop does not interrupt a send that is already in progress. There is no chunking, progress display, playlist, per-cycle re-read, file-change monitoring, or mid-file cancellation.

Send File (Raw)

Send File (Raw) reads a selected file in the Rust backend and transmits its exact bytes. Empty files are rejected. There is no UTF-8 conversion, newline conversion, or hex-text parsing: a file containing AA 55 sends 41 41 20 35 35. File TX excludes other TX and Sequence operations until it finishes. This first version reads the complete file into memory and has no progress, cancellation, chunk delay, XMODEM, or YMODEM support.

Terminal display modes

The terminal keeps up to 5000 TX/RX entries in memory. Display Mode offers Events (Hex, lossy UTF-8 Text with escaped controls, or Both) and Continuous RX (Text or Hex). Switching modes only rerenders stored raw bytes; it never sends data, reconnects, changes the Send Text/Hex format, or changes the Auto TX payload. Events keep separate TX/RX rows; TX rows use their existing Hex format. Clear View only clears the on-screen history. It does not clear device buffers or affect the connection.

Continuous RX Text retains the former Stream presentation: RX-only content without direction badges or event rows. RX fragments concatenate without event-boundary line breaks; LF creates a newline and CR is omitted. Other control characters remain escaped, and the streaming UTF-8 decoder handles characters split across RX events. This is not an ANSI/VT100 terminal emulator. Continuous RX Hex joins received bytes across event boundaries as two-digit uppercase hex pairs with exactly one space between bytes; empty RX events add no separator. CR, LF, NUL, and non-text bytes are displayed literally as hex. Neither Continuous RX mode includes TX events, event labels, or timestamps.

Show TX defaults to On. Turning it Off hides TX rows in Events modes without affecting Send or stored history. The control is disabled in both Continuous RX modes without resetting its preference; the preference applies again upon returning to an Events mode. Sequence Result continues to offer only Hex, Text, and Both.

Terminal export

Export writes a snapshot of the current Terminal history in one of three formats. Terminal Log (Hex) preserves the existing human-readable uppercase hex transcript, one entry per line, for example TX 00 FF followed by RX 00 FF. RX Raw writes only received bytes to a .bin file. TX + RX Raw writes every TX and RX entry's bytes in history order to a .bin file. Raw exports contain no direction labels, separators, line endings, event boundaries, timestamps, or other metadata. Their default filenames include the local export time as YYYYMMDD_HHmmss.

Display Mode and Show TX only affect presentation and do not filter exports. RX Raw is unavailable until at least one RX byte exists. Clear View clears the current Terminal history, so cleared data is no longer available for any export. Entries evicted by the 5000-entry history limit are likewise unavailable. Export is a manual snapshot, not a continuous capture writer. TX + RX Raw is a flattened byte history and is not a protocol/session replay format; bytes that originally came from the device are transmitted as TX if that file is later sent with Send File (Raw).

Sequence

The editor supports Send Text, Send Bytes, Wait, Read, Read Until, and nested Repeat. Properties shows a short explanation for the selected step. New, Load, Save, Validate, Add Step, Add Child, Delete, Move Up, and Move Down remain available. Drafts may be temporarily invalid while editing. Validate, Save and Run use Core's unified Sequence v1 parser and validation.

Sequence files use transport: {type, settings}, not the legacy root serial. UART Sequence settings contain the original six line parameters. TCP Sequence settings contain only io_timeout_ms, never Host, Port or Connect Timeout. The device resource and execution mode are selected in Connection Setup.

New creates an empty UART or TCP draft according to the selected transport tab. Load keeps the JSON's own transport, including when it differs from the current tab. Save and Validate work without a connection. Copy from Connection Setup is available only when the editor transport matches the Connection Setup tab, and copies only the applicable settings (six UART line parameters or TCP I/O Timeout). Neither changing transport tabs nor copying changes the connection or automatically converts a loaded Sequence.

The editor shows Not connected, Settings match, or an explicit transport or settings mismatch. Run requires an active session of the same transport and matching settings: all six UART settings or the single TCP I/O Timeout. A mismatch disables Run and leaves the connection and draft intact. Core rechecks the match before executing the shared StepRunner and producing the existing result/transcript. The last result, including completed steps, raw-byte transcript, and failure partial bytes when available, is held only in application memory. The status and controls remain visible above a 250px scrollable area shared by Step Results and Transcript. Each new run starts at the top; switching RX display does not reset the scroll position. Save Result exports that complete result as JSON with its original byte arrays, regardless of RX display. Failed runs retain the failing step, error, completed results, transcript, and partial bytes when available. The button is disabled until a result exists. There is no saved run history or automatic result directory.

Troubleshooting and current limits

  • Cannot switch transport or edit settings: Disconnect first; connection/mode controls are locked during connection and execution.
  • Unexpected text: Inspect Hex. Raw bytes, not the display decoder, are authoritative.
  • No response after Text TX: Confirm whether the device needs CR/LF; Text TX does not add either automatically.
  • TCP does not connect: Check Host/IP and device Port, not an HTTP URL. TCP is a raw client without automatic reconnect.
  • Sequence Run is disabled: Validate the JSON and match its transport and settings to the active session.
  • Export unavailable: Exports use current in-memory Terminal history. Clear View and the 5000-event cap discard data from the export snapshot.
  • Send File or Sequence disabled during Auto TX: Stop Auto TX first.

There is no persistent run-history database, continuous disk capture, or protocol framing in this version.
